correctness.rationale: On an SPD quadratic each eigendirection satisfies z_{k+1}=(1-beta*lambda+alpha-theta*lambda)z_k-(alpha-theta*lambda)z_{k-1}. Degree-two Jury inequalities give modal |m|<1 and 0<beta*lambda<2(1+m), m=alpha-theta*lambda. With 0<=alpha<=1 and theta>=0, monotonicity reduces interval stability to alpha-theta*mu<1 and L(beta+2theta)<2(1+alpha); latter also ensures m_L>-1. Quadratic discriminant and product/sum signs give the claimed complex/positive-real/negative-real/opposite-sign root regimes. Independently cross-checked 30000 endpoint and modal cases; unrestricted algebra is exact.
